Existing core-profile repositories receive the wrapper on their next automatic workflow sync." (from the PR description / changelog entry).
  Expected change site: `workflow-templates/profiles/core.txt` and `tests/test_update_workflows_guardrails.py`

The `standard` list is built as `core[:-1] + ["ai-orchestrate.yml", "ai-orchestrate-poll.yml", core[-1], "ai-validate.yml", "ai-sync-labels.yml", "review_rb_judge_dispatch.yml"]`, which produces 12 entries matching the unchanged `workflow-templates/profiles/standard.txt` order (verified by reading the file). README.md (lines 989-1011) and agents.md (line 779) were updated to mention the seven-wrapper core profile; the changelog fragment `changelog.d/6262-clarify-respond-standalone.md` gained a sentence documenting the new delivery. Task is complete against the PR description.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
- Requirement: "Record memory candidate after auto-answer now runs only when an answer was actually posted (`SKIP_AUTO_ANSWER == 'false'`)." (proactive fix in PR description; gate is at `.github/workflows/orchestrate_clarify_respond.yml` line 1248-1253 of the PR head)
  Expected change site: `scripts/orchestrate_parse_and_post_answer.sh` (the helper that exports `SKIP_AUTO_ANSWER` into `$GITHUB_ENV`)
  Evidence of absence: Verified by reading the file directly. `SKIP_AUTO_ANSWER` is exported to `$GITHUB_ENV` at three points: line 268 (`SKIP_AUTO_ANSWER=true` when loop guard blocks or escalate was requested), line 276 (`SKIP_AUTO_ANSWER=true` when the command-claim was already taken), and line 317 (`SKIP_AUTO_ANSWER=false` when the `/answer` comment was successfully posted). The cross-pollination finding that the env var is undefined was based on a stale snapshot — the helper is staged from the verified workflow support checkout, the gate evaluates after the helper runs (because the new "Parse and post answer" step always gates on `(steps.run_codex.outcome != 'failure' || steps.standalone_fallback.outputs.ready == 'true')`), and the env-var defaults to "false" in the well-defined case. Not a gap.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
- tests/test_update_workflows_guardrails.py:47-63 | hardening suggestion
  PROBLEM: The new `standard = core[:-1] + [.., core[-1], ..]` construction re-uses `core[-1]` to keep the respond wrapper in the same position in `standard.txt` as before the core-profile change.
  WHY: The clever reuse is fragile: if a future PR appends another wrapper to `core` after `ai-orchestrate-clarify-respond.yml`, the new wrapper becomes `core[-1]` and silently displaces the respond wrapper from position 9 in `standard`, producing a wrong expected list that still passes the test.
  Suggested minimal fix: Hoist `"ai-orchestrate-clarify-respond.yml"` into a module-level constant (e.g. `RESPOND_WRAPPER = "ai-orchestrate-clarify-respond.yml"`) and reference it from both the `core` and the `standard` list. ~3 lines changed.
  Estimated lines changed: 3
  HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 2
